messages:
Alex: quick one — support reported a failed generate call and gave request_id=abc123 but console search returns no results. where else should I look?
Maria: is that the external request_id header or an internal req_id? sometimes the edge uses X-Request-Ref instead of X-Request-ID.
Alex: it came from the customer payload, they pasted `abc123`. i checked the console trace list and nothing matched.
Zach: start with the edge/ingress logs — most of the time the header is added by the proxy. try stern for the last 10m across ingress pods: 
```
stern -n prod 'ingress' --since 10m | rg "abc123" -n
```
Maria: if stern returns nothing, check the gateway logs (label app=gateway): 
```
kubectl logs -n prod -l app=gateway --tail=500 | rg "abc123"
```
Jen: also search for the trace id if support provided it. console sometimes drops the header but the trace exists. you can search traces for a span with that request id in tag/attributes.
observability-bot: Tip: Console hides some indexed fields in compact view — expand the raw event or click "show headers" in the trace to confirm header name.
Zach: if you only have a trace id (e.g., 1a2b3c), you can map trace->request with the trace link in console or with kusto/es: `service_traces | where traceId=="1a2b3c"` (internal query).
Alex: any quick grep/jq trick if logs are JSON?
Maria: yep — stream the pod logs and pipe to jq, example for nginx-ingress: 
```
kubectl logs ingress-abc -n prod --tail=200 | jq -r 'select(.headers).headers["x-request-ref"]' | rg "abc123"
```
Jen: if the request hit the edge and was proxied, also check the edge-to-backend hop logs — sometimes the request_id is rewritten on the server-to-server call. search for the path + timestamp window.
Alex: good call. what about when console shows a trace but "link to logs" is missing?
Zach: that usually means logs landed in a shard console doesn't index. fallback: grab the trace's span that contains the pod name, then kubectl logs directly on that pod with the time window.
Maria: shorthand: find span -> note pod/service -> kubectl logs -n prod <pod> --since=2m | rg "abc123"
observability-bot: Hint: add `--follow` to stern if you want to watch new matches. also consider `--context` to include surrounding lines for easier debugging.
Alex: perfect — i'll try stern -> gateway -> pod logs chain, and ping here if stuck. thanks :pray:
Jen: ping me if you need a quick dashboard link, I can drop the per-route logs dashboard for the time range.
Alex: thank you all, updating the ticket now :thumbsup:
